To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the probabilistic guarantee is a function of the temporal dependence of the demand process and that it decreases in the temporal dependence of demand.

the probabilistic guarantee for the data-driven newsvender problem depends on the underlying temporal dependence structure and that the dependence is captured through a lower bound on a probability that depends on the correlation coefficient of a specific linear time series model that is fitted to the data.
the near-optimality guarantee depends on the underlying temporal dependence and the near optimality probability decreases as the underlying temporal dependence increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
providing a probabilistic near optimality guarantee for the data-driven newsviper with temporally dependent and unknown demand.
the development and analysis of a novel Monte Carlo approach for data-driven inventory optimization.
the question of whether a data-driven newsvender with temporally dependent and unknown marginal demand can perform nearly optimally.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for stationary and temporally independent demand, the probabilistic guarantee is the same regardless of the marginal distribution function of the demand.
, for a given level of near optimality, the probabilistic guarantee of the data-driven newsviper is worse than that of the independent case but is better than that of the dependent case.
the probabilistic guarantees of the data-driven inventory-target estimates are more favorable in the presence of temporal dependence than in the case of independent demand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the near optimality guarantees for the data-driven newsviper with dependent demand are not as strong as the independent and identically distributional demand.
the near optimality guarantee is not only a function of the sample size, the target fill-rate, and the underlying demand distribution, but also a function of the temporal dependence.
the near optimality guarantees for temporally dependent demand are more conservative than for independent demand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the probabilistic guarantee is not sensitive to the underlying temporal dependence structure, as long as it is stationary.
temporal dependence can be exploited in a data-driven inventory-target estimation problem to improve upon the probabilistic guarantee, and thus to reduce the inventory risk.
temporal dependence in the demand process can lead to a more stringent guarantee, i.e., a larger sample size requirement.
